links.outcome: Active documentation time in notes, AI-scribed vs unassisted, within physician
links.effect: Median active time 10.0 vs 12.5 min (-2.4 min adjusted); notes about 14% longer (+629 characters); completion not delayed (-6 minutes).
links.quote: Among emergency physicians, AI scribe use was associated with less active time in the note, deferred note-start, and longer notes, without delaying completion or increasing short-term returns, with effect sizes consistent with ambulatory randomized data.

links.outcome: 72-hour ED return and note completion lag as downstream safety and workflow signals
links.effect: Note completion not delayed (-6 minutes); 72-hour ED return not increased (-0.8 percentage point; 95% CI -1.5 to -0.1).
links.quote: Note completion was not delayed (-6 minutes), and 72-hour ED return was not increased (-0.8 percentage point; 95% confidence interval -1.5 to -0.1).

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of real-world deployment of ambient AI scribes across 20 emergency departments measuring documentation time and patient safety outcomes.
